tier_reason: Upgraded from B: every dusty number matches site/data/results/dusty.json and the nginx, drogon, hical, h2o, mongoose and libreactorng rows match their sibling JSON files; the benchmark code is public in MDA2AV/HttpArena (frameworks/dusty/Dockerfile, frameworks/nginx/Dockerfile, frameworks/drogon/Dockerfile, scripts/benchmark.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh, scripts/lib/framework.sh), compilers and flags for both sides are in the Dockerfiles, and the CPU model (AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX) is in site/data/current.json, the same basis on which wtx and cutelyst on this harness were tiered A in wave 5.

corrections.claimed_speedup: HttpArena, same harness but separate runs: baseline-4096 dusty 3,309,488 req/s vs nginx (C) 3,284,513 (+0.8%, derived from page data, a tie), Hical (C++) 3,228,043 (1.03x, derived), Drogon (C++) 2,022,710 (1.64x, derived); behind h2o (C) 3,641,609, mongoose (C) 3,707,598 and libreactorng (C) 4,377,377. json-tls-4096: 989,946 vs Drogon 253,055 (3.91x, derived) and Hical 549,765 (1.80x, derived), but behind nginx 1,313,755, h2o 1,229,462 and mongoose 1,102,964. json-comp-4096: 397,047 vs Drogon 127,466 (3.11x, derived) and Hical 261,955 (1.52x, derived). limited-conn-4096: 1,930,687, ahead of Drogon 1,694,883 but behind nginx 2,626,297, Hical 2,407,681 and h2o 2,651,569. pipelined-4096 (reference-only profile, excluded from the composite score): 4,379,900 vs nginx 4,037,345, but behind Drogon 7,801,404, Hical 4,851,267 and h2o 4,938,603.
corrections.hardware: HttpArena dedicated machine: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), performance governor (site/data/current.json). The server container is pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 cores plus SMT siblings) and the load generator runs on the remaining cores (scripts/lib/profiles.sh).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: dusty: Zig 0.16.0, target x86_64-linux-musl, zig build --release=fast -Dcpu=x86_64_v3+aes+pclmul+adx (frameworks/dusty/Dockerfile). nginx 1.31.4 with the custom C handler module ngx_http_httparena_module.c, configured with --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG' on Debian trixie build-essential (frameworks/nginx/Dockerfile). Drogon: CMake Release build of main.cc on the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image, run with LD_PRELOAD=libjemalloc.so.2 (frameworks/drogon/Dockerfile). Server containers run with --security-opt seccomp=unconfined and unlimited memlock (scripts/lib/framework.sh), so io_uring is available.
corrections.caveats: Not faster than the strongest C servers: a tie with nginx on baseline-4096 (+0.8%), behind nginx on limited-conn-4096 (1,930,687 vs 2,626,297) and json-tls-4096 (989,946 vs 1,313,755), and behind h2o (3,641,609), mongoose (3,707,598) and libreactorng (4,377,377) on baseline-4096. The clear wins are over the C++ frameworks Drogon (1.64x baseline, 3.91x json-tls, 3.11x json-comp) and Hical (1.03x baseline, 1.80x json-tls); on the pipelined profile Drogon (7,801,404) is 1.78x faster than dusty (derived from page data). Rows come from separate runs on the same machine: dusty.json was saved on 2026-10-07 (PR #1529, dusty 0.4), nginx.json last changed on 2026-08-30 and drogon.json on 2026-09-06, so the nginx tie is within run-to-run noise. The dusty entry is maintained by the dusty author (meta.json maintainers: lalinsky); handlers on all sides are minimal benchmark handlers (nginx is a custom C module; Drogon is built on an unpinned image). The baseline profile mixes GET and POST with query parsing, not static files. The dusty README itself makes no comparison with C or C++ servers.
corrections.why_faster: Runtime and I/O backend, not Zig codegen: the zio runtime uses io_uring (allowed by the suite's seccomp=unconfined containers) while nginx uses epoll; the margin over Drogon reflects Drogon framework overhead (it also trails nginx, h2o and Hical on baseline). No mechanism analysis from the authors.

notes: Numbers and metadata (MIT, 145 stars, last commit 2026-10-11, not a fork, not archived) confirmed; tier raised to A on the HttpArena precedent. Record as shortcomings: ties nginx and loses to h2o, mongoose, libreactorng on baseline and to nginx on limited-conn and json-tls; wins only over Drogon and Hical; Drogon beats it 1.78x on pipelined; cross-run rows (dusty 2026-10-07 vs nginx 2026-08-30); win comes from io_uring vs epoll, not the language.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: TechEmpower frameworks/Rust/faf/faf.dockerfile (HEAD): base image errantmind/debian-faf:v3 (nightly rustc, version not stated), clang-15 and ld.lld-15, RUSTFLAGS -Ctarget-cpu=native -Ztune-cpu=native -Zmutable-noalias=yes -Copt-level=3 -Clto=thin -Ccodegen-units=1 -Cpanic=abort -Coverflow-checks=no -Cdebug-assertions=no, cargo build --release -Zbuild-std; the faf crate is pulled from git HEAD (unpinned). corrections.caveats: At Round 22 faf was listed as Realistic/Platform (IA column 'Rea' on the screenshot); TechEmpower PR #10608 (2026-01-23, under issue #9578 'No more fakes') reclassified it as Stripped because it hardcodes HTTP headers: the TFB src/main.rs copies a constant status line, Server, Content-Type and Content-Length block, then the cached date and the body, after checking only the method and path. lithium (Realistic, Micro) and cinatra (Realistic, Fullstack) run real frameworks, so faf does less work per request. Plaintext at the top of the table is saturated: the first nine rows are within 0.3% and the first 19 within 6%, network and pipelining bound, so the ordering among them is noise, not a language effect. The faf README claims design choices were 'meticulously benchmarked' but names no competitors and gives no numbers; the no_std variant is said to be about 1% slower. Last commit 2024-04-14 (stale). Drogon does not appear in the top 50 screenshot.
corrections.why_faster: Not established: at the 10 GbE plaintext ceiling the top entries tie, and faf's handler copies a precomputed response after checking only method and path (TechEmpower PR #10608 reclassified it as Stripped), so any margin over the Realistic C++ frameworks reflects less work, not Rust codegen. The design uses unsafe Rust with no dependencies and raw epoll (README).

The full-codec 'firenio' entry ranks 34 at 5,613,390, 0.80x lithium (derived from page data), so the realistic codec is slower than the C++ baselines. The firenio README links the TechEmpower results but gives no figures. -XX:+AggressiveOpts is deprecated in JDK 11. Last commit 2021-10-12 (abandoned). Drogon does not appear in the top 50 screenshot.
corrections.why_faster: Not established as a language effect: a tie at the 10 GbE plaintext ceiling. Reaching it relies on the lite decoder (request line plus Content-Length only), cached URL lookup, per-event-loop write batching, pooled unsafe buffers and a native epoll transport (TFB TestHttpLoadServer.java and firenio-codec HttpCodec.java); the full-codec firenio entry is 0.80x lithium.
